findings.claim: The NETFRAMEWORK half of every new preprocessor guard suppresses ExcludeFromCodeCoverage even on supported .NET Framework targets where System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists (it has been available since .NET Framework 4.0). Consequently, generated code for targets such as net472 remains included in coverage, although the requirement calls for conditional omission only where the attribute is unavailable.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageNetFrameworkRequirementsTests.GeneratedTypesAreDecoratedOnNetFramework. It generates and compiles the output against the .NET Framework 4.7.2 reference assemblies with NETFRAMEWORK defined, then asserts that every generated type has an active ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute. The current guards make all such attributes inactive, so the test fails on head.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decorate every type emitted by all formatter and resolver templates, including nested caches and helper classes, wherever the BCL attribute is available. Emission is always on by default and no setting is added; conditional compilation is used only for targets lacking the attribute.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Limit the required decorations to the generated formatter classes themselves, leaving resolver classes and their nested helpers undecorated, and add an opt-out MSBuild setting that suppresses the formatter attributes when requested while preserving decoration by default.
